newsitem.title: KENYA: "Mo" Amin negotiated with hijackers before crash.
newsitem.headline: "Mo" Amin negotiated with hijackers before crash.

text.p: Award-winning Kenyan cameraman Mohamed "Mo" Amin, one of the 125 fatal victims of last week's Ethiopian Airlines disaster, was negotiating with the hijackers in the minutes before the Boeing 767 crashed into the sea, a survivor said on Thursday.

Monica Tibwitta told Reuters that Amin, with either one or two other passengers in the plane's first-class section, stood up shortly after the pilot told passengers he had virtually no more fuel and they should prepare for a crash landing.

"I remember when the pilot announced about the emergency landing, he (Amin) stood up and started talking to the hijackers and tried to negotiate with them," Tibwitta said by telephone from her bed in the private Nairobi Hospital.
The 27-year-old Ugandan, who works for Coca-Cola in Kenya, survived with a broken arm and bruises after the plane crashed into the sea just off a luxury tourist hotel in the Comoro Islands.
She was sitting in the third row in business class and was able to see through into the first-class area where two of the three hijackers stayed throughout the hijacking.
"I think one or two other passengers also stood up and tried to negotiate," she said.
Survivors in Nairobi, questioned by Reuters this week, say about 15 minutes elapsed between the pilot's crash warning and the plane's entry into the Indian Ocean.
Tibwitta said she did not recognise Amin at first but was told who he was by other passengers watching the negotiations, which were inaudible from the business class area.
The 53-year-old Amin, a British citizen of Asian origin born in Kenya, was buried in Nairobi's Moslem cemetery on Wednesday before hundreds of mourners.
In a 40-year career as photojournalist, cameraman and businessman, Amin will be remembered most for the images he took of the Ethiopian famine in 1984.
